item.title: ‘Rare,’ ‘That Does Not Deserve a Double Bang’: Fans Debate Mike Breen’s Call as Mikal Bridges Sinks Buzzer-Beater to Beat Trail Blazers
item.description: Mikal Bridges © Imagn Mikal Bridges came to the rescue for the New York Knicks when he drained a buzzer-beating 3 to give his team a 97-96 win over the Portland Trail Blazers. On the local commentary team, play-by-play announcer Mike Breen made a rare “Bang, bang” call to punctuate Bridges’ clutch shot. As a testament to Breen’s iconic commentary, the “double bang” call became a subject of dispute among fans on social media. Some fans weren’t in favor of Breen using this special call on this occasion, while others were simply hyped. “That does not deserve a double bang,” one fan tweeted . Breen, a recipient of the Basketball Hall of Fame’s Curt Gowdy Media Award, has made the “Bang, bang” call on only a few occasions. These include game-winners from Steph Curry and Luka Doncic. Bridges’ heroics in the clutch sent Madison Square Garden into a frenzy, but earlier in the game, it didn’t appear that a buzzer-beater would be necessary. The Knicks led by as many as 26 points, but Damian Lillard and Donovan Clingan spearheaded a Blazers comeback. Two free throws by Deni Avdija with less than four seconds left gave the Blazers their only lead of the night. Portland appeared to have stolen a game from the Knicks on their home floor. But on the final possession, Josh Hart found his old Villanova teammate near the left wing. Bridges drove, took a step back to free himself of Toumani Camara’s defense, and made the shot as time expired. “We Do It for Those Guys”: Mikal Bridges Gives a Shoutout to Former Knicks Players After Sinking Game-Winner at MSG Mikal Bridges’ clutch shot came on Homecoming Night at the Garden. In attendance were former Knicks players like Walt “Clyde” Frazier, Earl “The Pearl” Monroe, Nate Robinson, and J.R. Smith. In his post-game interview, Bridges gave a shoutout to these Knicks of yesteryear. “We do it for those guys. Happy we could do this on their night.” Saturday also happened to be Monroe’s 82nd birthday. For the Basketball Hall of Famer, a birthday present came in the form of a game-winning shot. item.description: EDITOR'S NOTE: In marking the Browns ' 80th birthday , we present 10 vignettes that help define each 10-year period , along with eight " Story of the Decade " articles. This is the "Story of the Decade" for the franchise's third-10-year period, 1966-75. Put yourself in Mike Phipps’ cleats. You barely missed a Heisman Trophy as a "Cradle of Quarterbacks" college star. An NFL team viewed you as its franchise QB, but to get you had to fork over one of the most popular figures in its history. You arrived as Led Zeppelin's "Whole Lotta Love" lit up WMMS-FM, in the 25th season of the Browns' classic history. The previous 24 produced 15 appearances in league championship games. "Stairway to Heaven" wasn't about you. You didn't turn into Otto Graham (105-17-4 record as Cleveland's starting QB), or Milt Plum (33-16), or Frank Ryan (52-22-2), or Bill Nelsen (34-16-1). Your record (24-25-2), your interceptions (81) and your placid persona made you a B-side disappointment as the franchise magic cracked. Michael Elston Phipps disappeared from Cleveland 50 years ago and for the most part was never heard from again. He did surface on camera with a gray head of hair in 2022, accompanied by his former college teammate Don Kiepert. “This is Purdue” interviewer Kate Young asked about his Browns days. “Have you ever been booed?” Phipps said. On Jan. 27, 1970, NFL Commissioner Pete Rozelle carried "the card" to a podium at the Belmont Plaza Hotel in New York City. Imagine if he had said: “With the first pick in the NFL draft, the Pittsburgh Steelers select Mike Phipps, quarterback, Purdue.” Phipps to Pittsburgh would have made sense. The Steelers' actual No. 1 pick, Terry Bradshaw, was erratic at Louisiana Tech. His last game brought a 34-14 loss to East Tennessee State in the Grantland Rice Bowl. item.description: Good morning! Go for nothing but net today. Coming up: 🏈 Big Ten bananas 🏆 Current’s championship ⚽ Poch’s first United match Madness: Big Ten day of chaos It always happens like this: At the moment when we least expect it, college football reaches out and shakes us with a Saturday that stuns the season. On a day with just one ranked-versus-ranked matchup (No. 1 Georgia 34, No. 21 South Carolina 6), we got nine hours of national chaos. The most shocking results occurred in the Big Ten. The day began with perhaps the sport’s most jaw-dropping moment of all: Matt Rhule’s Nebraska beat a ranked opponent in the form of No. 14 Ohio State, 31-28. That snapped a 31-game ranked losing streak that dated back to 2016, and came on the tail of some maddeningly close losses to prestigious opponents (Indiana and Oregon) earlier this season. The Buckeyes will need to beat Michigan to finish 8-4, but even that would mean a disaster of a year under Ryan Day. Then came two different upsets, both in overtime: Michigan 18, No. 4 UCLA 16. This one took three overtimes, as the unbeaten Bruins lost both the game and their quarterback, Ty Dieffenbach (who himself was already a backup). That Michigan would win was far from a shock, given its elite defense. But the unit gave up a late tying drive before knocking Dieffenbach out of the game during the first play of OT. Third-stringer Madden Iamaleava (the sophomore brother of injured starter Nico) was way out of his depth as the game continued: UCLA did not get a first down after Dieffenbach’s injury. Washington 27, No. 8 Indiana 24. The Huskies blocked two Indiana field goals, including the tying attempt in overtime. The Hoosiers have been breaking down for weeks but kept winning close games … until now. Additional injuries on the offensive line, at linebacker and potentially at wideout will make everything even harder. item.title: 3 keys to a Jets win at the Chargers in Week 11
item.description: The New York Jets (2-8) will face the Los Angeles Chargers (1-8) in Week 11 at SoFi Stadium. The Jets will be looking to snap a five game losing streak and also break a pathetic streak of no touchdowns from the offense in nine quarters. The Chargers finally got their first win of the season this past Monday night, defeating the Baltimore Ravens 23-20. For both teams, it’s also a bit of a dilemma on whether winning this game is a bad thing. A win for either team means they will drop in the draft order, which will frustrate fans of both teams looking for a high draft pick in the first round. For the Jets, a win may be an easier pill to swallow as they have three first-round picks in the 2027 draft, including the Colts pick acquired last year in the Sauce Gardner trade. Here are Jets Wire's three Key matchups for Week 11 : David Bailey vs. Travis Burke While Bailey’s numbers on the scoresheet weren’t very impressive last week, he still managed to make some plays including almost intercepting a Josh Allen screen pass for a touchdown. He only had one tackle against the Bills last week and the defense suffers when he's not able to get after the quarterback. With Bailey lining up on the left side, he’ll match up against Burke, who is massive at 6’9", 315 lbs. Burke was selected in the fourth round of the 2026 draft and has been pretty steady on the right side of the offensive line. He does struggles with pass blocking, where he ranks at the bottom of the league. He's allowed 22 pressures and a sack on the season. Bailey is tied for seventh in the league with 7.5 sacks and if he can generate enough pressure on Burke, he could make like miserable for Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert all afternoon on Sunday. And I could be in the minority here, but I see none of the leadership qualities that were on display throughout his time with the New Orleans Saints . The Jets did a poor job addressing their linebacking unit in free agency as well as the draft and it’s coming back to haunt them in a big way. Davis is a major liability on the field, especially on passing downs. However, they have such little depth, they have no choice but to play him. item.title: One fan claims Texas senator-elect James Talarico got booed during Longhorns appearance
item.description: Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images James Talarico will take office this January, but before that, he made an appearance at a Texas Longhorns game, where the reception was reportedly less than stellar. Talarico won the senatorial race in Texas against Ken Paxton, becoming the first Democratic senator-elect in the state since 1993. However, even with his resounding victory in the midterm elections, Talarico may not have received the positive response many would have expected when he made an appearance at the Texas Longhorns game. Did James Talarico get booed at Texas Longhorns game? A video of James Talarico appearing and waving at the crowd during a Texas Longhorns game went viral on social media. However, there were many in the comments on the video who suggested that the video had been layered with music to drown out the sound of the senator-elect being booed. One fan wrote: “Had to add music because he was booed!” However, another fan quickly clarified that this wasn’t the case, noting: “I was there, and this is a lie. He received overwhelming cheers, particularly from “Bo French’s student section“. He is a Longhorn grad who just beat the brakes off Paxton.” A third fan who was in attendance as well made the same point: “Our whole section was cheering. Don’t know what these other people were watching.” However, a simple search of game footage showed that Talarico didn’t receive any major negative response when he was shown on the big screen at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday. Given the recent negative reception that Senator Ted Cruz received when attending a Longhorns game, the narrative that Talarico also got booed may have a political element to it. item.title: “Karma For Him,” “Should’ve Stayed at Ole Miss”: CFB Fans React As Lane Kiffin Picks Up Unwanted 35-Year Old Record at LSU After Tennessee Loss
item.description: LSU head coach Lane Kiffin. © IMAGN via Reuters Connect LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin finds himself in the middle of a disappointing season. LSU lost Saturday’s game against the Tennessee Volunteers, marking the program’s fifth loss of the season, with four coming against ranked opponents. Kiffin also became the first LSU coach since Curley Hallman to lose four or more SEC games in his debut season. Hallman finished 3-4 in conference play during his first season in 1991. Before Hallman, Gaynell Tinsley had suffered five SEC defeats in his debut season in 1948. Fans shared their thoughts on LSU’s latest loss under Kiffin. “Karma for Kiffin right now,” one fan said. “They’re not gonna make him give back any money, so it panned out perfectly for him,” one fan wrote. “Ahhh, that’s how you ruin a program with name RECOGNITION 😂 hire Lane Kiffin,” one fan noted. “Should have stayed at Ole Miss,” one fan commented. “Saw this coming from a mile away,” one fan added. After the latest loss against No. 9 Tennessee, Kiffin’s record against AP Top-10 opponents dropped to 6-20. His road record against those teams is even worse at 1-10, including eight consecutive defeats. He is also winless in four games against top-10 opponents this season. What’s Left For Lane Kiffin’s LSU After Tennessee Exposed Sam Leavitt & Co. Saturday’s loss was a result of LSU’s ineffective offense, led by quarterback Sam Leavitt. In the 27-13 loss, the Tigers allowed eight sacks and 13 tackles for loss. Leavitt completed 27 of 39 passes for 222 yards, and LSU managed only 43 rushing yards. According to CBS Sports , the Tigers committed three turnovers and 16 penalties, their highest penalty total in a game since 1995. LSU has one regular-season game remaining against Arkansas on Nov. 28. item.title: Verstappen a constant amid chaos as he says Russell is 'so far below my level'
item.description: Max Verstappen has won three of the four Las Vegas Grands Prix [Press Association] Warning: This article contains offensive language Max Verstappen was a constant amid the chaos at a remarkable Las Vegas Grand Prix. He was the star figure in a race that had 34 overtaking moves for the lead in 50 laps and 352 overall, in which the biggest advantage the leader ever had was 1.5 seconds, and in which there were five cars fighting nose to tail for the lead to the final lap, and for much of the race many more than that. Even better for Verstappen, George Russell made a critical mistake 24 hours after he had revived his long-standing, on-off spat with the Dutchman. Russell, who had been Verstappen's main threat from the start of the race, locked up his brakes and speared into the barrier trying to pass Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli for second place behind Verstappen with two laps to go. Verstappen said: "He speaks a lot next to the track, and it doesn't really bother me because he's so far below my level that it doesn't really make any sense for me anyway to try and challenge that, you know? "And today, karma is a bitch. It was honestly fantastic when I looked in my mirror and I saw what was happening. I was, like, "Fantastic, my day is only getting better." "And of course, when I then crossed the line in first, my day was complete." Verstappen wins extraordinary race as Ferraris collide Hamilton-Leclerc collision 'completely unacceptable' Verstappen felt motivated to make these remarks because of what Russell had said the day before. After an on-track altercation in practice, the pair had had an exchange of views in the stewards' room. Then, after Verstappen took pole from Russell - after fastest man Antonelli's five-place penalty was taken into account - the Briton took a pop at the Dutchman. "I am not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they are bigger and better than everyone else," Russell said. "Somebody has got to stand up to that guy." In the paddock, a number of people felt that Verstappen was probably not the right "guy" to pick a fight with. Even though Russell was fighting with Verstappen throughout the race, the nature of their drives was different. Russell would pass the Red Bull on the straight. Then Verstappen would reclaim the lead in more extreme fashion, on the outside of the fast kink leading on to the pit straight, or on the outside again at the long Turn Three. Hardly anyone else even tried these moves, let alone pulled them off. Verstappen made them look routine. After his error, Russell managed to extricate himself from the crash barrier, but he had turned a certain podium finish into a ninth place. It was the perfect encapsulation of a season in which almost nothing has gone right. For Verstappen, it was almost too good to be true. item.title: Pontypool front row inducted into hall of fame
item.description: Graham Price, Bobby Windsor and Charlie Faulkner won a total of 88 Wales caps between them [Getty Images] Individually they were wonderfully talented but together, they were fearsome. The Pontypool front row of Tony 'Charlie' Faulkner, Bobby Windsor and Graham Price would become the stuff of rugby legend. The trio were the bulwark of a ferocious club side, the all-conquering Wales team of the Seventies and the British and Irish Lions. Now, 43 years after Price retired, the last of the trio to do so, they have become the 187th, 188th and 189th inductees of World Rugby's Hall of Fame. "Rugby is often referred to as the ultimate team sport," said John Eales, chairman of the Hall of Fame panel. "And yet, within every team there are often units that, through their dominance, style and standards, transcend generations. "The Pontypool front row were one such unit. Playing in many great Pontypool, Welsh and British and Irish Lions teams, Graham Price, Bobby Windsor and Charlie Faulkner stood out as individuals but excelled as a unit." In January 1975, against France, the trio became the first entire front row from the same club to start a Wales game. They would go on to play a total of 19 times for Wales as a unit, losing just four of those games. As a unit they twice enjoyed Five Nations Grand Slam success for Wales in 1976 and 1978, either side of a Lions tour to New Zealand in 1977. So well known - and feared - the trio were referred to as the 'Viet Gwent' in a song called Up and Under, Here We Go by popular Welsh entertainer Max Boyce. Price played a record 12 successive Test for the Lions. Faulkner died in February 2023, aged 81, though his nephew Lyndon was appointed chairman of the Welsh Rugby Union in November.

item.title: Takeaways from Maryland football’s 35-21 loss to No. 18 USC
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 21: Quarterback Malik Washington #7 of the Maryland Terrapins rolls out to pass as defensive tackles Tomuhini "Tom Tom" Topui Jr. #52 and Jaimeon Winfield #45 chase in pursuit during the fourth quarter at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum on November 21, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Kevin Terrell/Getty Images) | Getty Images Maryland football brought a two-game winning streak to the West Coast for a matchup with No. 18 USC. Despite that fact, it was a major surprise when the Terps entered halftime up a point on the hosts. But on a day where several stunning upsets happened across the Big Ten, the Terps couldn’t hang onto any Hollywood magic of their own. The Trojans stormed back and scored 22 unanswered points to open the second half, as Maryland repeatedly neutralized its own hopes at making a comeback. Here are three takeaways from the Terps’ road finale. Defense can’t catch a break Maryland’s defense had made a habit of bending without breaking under interim head coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim’s tutelage. The Terps continued to get gashed in man coverage following the leadership change, but twice against Wisconsin and four times against Purdue, Maryland stopped its opponents within the final 25 yards, forcing a field goal. It initially appeared that trend would continue in California, but as the Terps stayed on the field longer and longer, the defense visibly wore down. By the end of the game, Maryland couldn’t keep up with the West Coast offense. Out of the first 24 minutes of the game, Maryland possessed the ball for just 6:15. However, that appeared to be more of an issue of the defense being caught asleep early. item.title: Sam Bennett, Linemates Put on a Show for the Panthers. Good Thing, Eh
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect SUNRISE — Sam Bennett got his second hat trick of the season for the Florida Panthers in Saturday’s win against the Buffalo Sabres. The story, however, was the play of Bennett’s line. At least according to Paul Maurice . “They don’t get a lot of notice because of some of the other names,” Maurice said, “but that’s a win on one line tonight, and they deserve all the credit for it.” Hard to argue. Bennett scored Florida’s first three goals in Florida’s eventual 4-3 win against the Sabres — but it was Sandis Vilmanis who netted the game-winner late in the third. Bennett’s shot from the slot appeared to hit Vilmanis with the puck dropping to the ice. Vilmanis turned on it and beat Alex Lyon giving the Bennett/Vilmanis/ Eetu Luostarinen line a hand in all four goals. The trio combined for four goals and three assists. Not too shabby. “Sometimes you feel like you have a little extra jump in your step,” Bennett said. “I thought our whole line was feeling really good tonight. We were moving well. It was fun to play with them. Lots of speed and direct plays and yeah, I think we found some chemistry there.’’ Maurice was not as thrilled with the rest of his team’s play saying the only redeeming thing to come from the win — aside from the victory itself — was the play of Bennett’s line and goalie Jacob Markstrom . Florida struggled to handle the puck, their lackluster clearing attempts leading to Buffalo’s second goal which gave the Sabres a 2-1 lead. A lot of stuff Maurice did not like will be addressed today when the team practices at the arena as part of the team’s annual PanthersFest. “We have an opportunity to be a better hockey team against Ottawa,’’ Maurice said. “And we will be a better hockey team.” Still, a win is a win. And, the team made a little bit of history. Or at least Bennett did. With his second hat trick of the season, Bennett gave Florida its sixth such game in 24 games. The last NHL team to have six hat tricks before Game 25 was the Pittsburgh Penguins in 1991-92. The Panthers have, at times, had trouble scoring. Other times, the goals have come in bunches. “It definitely makes it fun,’’ Bennett said. “Obviously, hat tricks aren’t the goal. The goal is to get wins, but obviously, it you know feels good and have a bunch of different guys who got them. Amid this uncertainty, former ESPN analyst Jemele Hill has pointed out one ‘great’ thing about the situation. item.title: Goals, goals, goals: Die Roten Bullen charge onwards and upwards
item.description: Goals, goals, goals: Die Roten Bullen charge onwards and upwards Registering seven victories and not a single stalemate, RB Leipzig coach Martin Demichelis has refined a successful formula by combining abundant energy with merciless finishing. Even at the rear, numbers stack up well when you exclude six conceded at the Allianz Arena – Luis Díaz was quite simply unplayable that day and fully deserved his hat-trick. So, take that domestic drubbing out of the equation and the defence has been breached eight times. Borussia Dortmund, boasting one of the best backlines in Europe, have conceded a league-best seven. Sitting in fourth position, Leipzig remain within three points of the current leaders in black and yellow. Some might say that the most controversial club in German football has gone under the radar up until now, at least to those looking casually from the outside in. Unbeaten at the Red Bull Arena with an impressive 15-point haul from five outings, the stadium has become an impenetrable fortress. Of course, the biggest challenges on home soil await: one a week before Christmas and the other in February. If we look back at the summer’s revolving door, a seemingly irreplaceable Yan Diomande left to ply his trade under José Mourinho. Xaver Schlager, troublesome and tenacious on any pitch, joined Nottingham Forest. Neil El Aynaoui and Rocco Reitz have plugged that Austrian gap, while Brajan Gruda – currently on loan from Brighton but joining permanently for approximately €30 million next year – has filled the void left by a certain Ivorian. Antonio Nusa quite rightly continues to attract interest from elsewhere, yet the club’s ability to identify talent and provide the right platform alleviates concerns on that front ahead of the January transfer window. With the mid-week Champions League visit of Lens approaching, internal focus now understandably shifts as much-needed points are on offer. One win and three defeats – the latter coming against heavyweight opposition – leave them in 29th place, although it has to be said that Europe is not where Demichelis and his men will be judged.

item.title: Real Madrid yet to make a final decision on former academy gem’s €80 million return
item.description: Real Madrid yet to make a final decision on former academy gem’s €80 million return According to Jose Felix Diaz of AS , Real Madrid have made no final decision regarding Nico Paz’s future yet. The Merengues are continuing to monitor the Argentine midfielder’s development at Como but will not rush into things as they consider whether to bring him back to the Santiago Bernabeu. Nico Paz can return for €80 million Real Madrid parted ways with Paz in 2024, selling him to Como while retaining a buyback clause for the three subsequent summer transfer windows. Los Blancos activated that clause to re-sign him from the Serie A outfit last summer, but sold him back to them for €60 million. Excelling in Italy (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) One of the major factors in that decision was the player’s own choice, as he wanted to stay with Como and continue playing regularly. However, as part of the agreement, Real Madrid secured another buyback clause for the Argentine prodigy, which will allow them to bring him back for a sum of €80 million in the summer of 2027. In fact, several outlets in Spain have suggested that Los Blancos have already decided to activate that clause and welcome the La Fabrica talent back to the Santiago Bernabeu before next season. No decision made Despite growing excitement around the 21-year-old, the possibility of a return to Real Madrid remains uncertain, and the Spanish giants are in no hurry to settle the matter. Real Madrid will not rush into a decision over Paz’s future. (Photo by Hernan Cortez/Getty Images) Real Madrid remain aware of Paz’s qualities, but they also understand that the player wants regular minutes and an important role in whichever team he represents. A return to his boyhood club would mean competing with established starters such as Jude Bellingham and Arda Guler, along with the likes of Rodrygo and Brahim Diaz for places. Real Madrid continue to follow his progress without rushing a decision, with the report suggesting that any call over Paz’s comeback could be made around spring. A fee of €80 million would be significant investment for the club and they will consider all possible factors, beyond just his form, before taking a final call on his return in the summer.

item.title: Takeaways from Maryland women’s basketball’s 109-39 win over Morgan State
item.description: No. 18 Maryland women’s basketball broke a program record for lowest number of points allowed against Morgan State in its 109-39 win on Saturday . Nine of the 10 Terps that played scored points and each one logged at least one rebound. Head coach Brenda Frese complimented the team’s unselfishness that led to the victory, noting that Saturday’s game will provide a good base for Maryland to develop as conference play approaches. “Every single person put some sort of mark in a record book,” Frese said. “[There were] some really good things for us to be able to build upon.” Here are three takeaways from Maryland’s win. Injuries moved minutes around, but quality of play stayed consistent Maryland starter Bri McDaniel and frequent sixth woman Lea Bartelme were both ruled out of Saturday’s game, forcing Frese to reframe the lineups. Jordyn Jackson significantly filled the space of the two injured guards. The freshman DMV native finished with 15 points, eight rebounds and four assists, all career highs. She attributed some of her success to team closeness. “I felt like me and my teammates played really [well] together,” Jackson said. “Our chemistry was there, and we’re just working really hard.” Chloe Sotell and Marya Boiko played their most well-rounded games of the year, combining for 16 points and eight rebounds. Boiko recorded her best field-goal percentage of the season, going 4-of-5 inside of the arc. Sotell’s two 3-pointers were the second-most on the team and she corralled five rebounds. Rainey Welson proved herself as a starter Rainey Welson earned her first career start against Morgan State, replacing McDaniel. She showed out, posting a career-high 18 points and knocking down a team-high four 3-pointers. Welson didn’t commit a foul in her 26 minutes of play, matching her career low. Frese intentionally picked Welson to join the starting lineup because of her versatility on the court. The sophomore guard had never played more than 23 minutes until Saturday. “[Welson] does so many things well for us,” Frese said. “She’s a really, really talented scorer…and defensively is in all the right places, whether we’re in man or zone.” Welson said that the 70-point win was gratifying, but not an excuse to stop pushing. “It’s rewarding,” Welson said. “But we want more than that. We want to win tough games […] our mindset’s forever forward.” The Terps improved their paint presence Maryland scored a season-high 66 points in the paint against Morgan State. The Terps went 33-of-40 on layups and scored 30 second-chance points, a notable improvement from their past four games. Oluchi Okanawa and Mimi Thiero each contributed five offensive rebounds, with Jackson and Nunu Agara adding four. Despite starting a four-guard lineup, the Terps tracked down 24 of their 34 missed shots. Defensive aggressiveness in the paint was on display as well. item.title: Did Springboks win change the narrative for Ireland?
item.description: Robert Baloucoune (right) scored two tries as Ireland beat South Africa in Dublin [Getty Images] Ten months out from the World Cup, Ireland needed to make a statement. They had lost their last six matches against South Africa, New Zealand and France, and questions were starting to be asked if this was an Irish team past their best. A year ago, South Africa had demolished the Irish scrum on their way to a 24-13 win in Dublin. But on Saturday, it was Ireland who came out on top with a 20-17 victory as Andy Farrell's side blocked out the pre-match noise after Rassie Erasmus' six-game ban. "We knew what a lot of the players were capable of, but for them to come out and do that just changes the narrative around the Irish rugby team," former Ireland scrum-half Conor Murray said on the Ireland Rugby Social podcast. "To do that to the world champions, and there were some whispers from the South Africans that they weren't great, but we made them look average with the physicality and the scrum. "Everyone looked so up for it. It changes the feeling of it." Ireland remind themselves that the best are beatable Farrell defends Prendergast after SA camp comments Former Ireland forward Mike McCarthy said it was a "phenomenal performance" as Robert Baloucoune scored two tries and Ronan Kelleher also crossed in Dublin. Despite having a mixed game with the boot, Sam Prendergast ultimately kicked the decisive points as Ireland held off a late fightback from the back-to-back world champions. "Everyone wrote them off pre-game. The boys have had to live with that for a year, when they capitulated at scrum time," he said. "All the talk was how South Africa were hurting after the France game and they would do it for Rassie, but it was phenomenal from every player." Speaking to the podcast after the game, Ireland back row Josh van der Flier said it was "one of those special days". "It's brilliant and the lads dug deep. South Africa are a brilliant side and everyone knows how good they are. "We worked unbelievably hard, and we're delighted to get the result." 'This could happen down the line' In contrast to the roar of 70,000 supporters in the Aviva, egged on by Ryan Baird at every scrum, Erasmus sat alone in South Africa's team hotel in Dublin. item.description: What is Mauricio Pochettino's best XI? It's a new dawn for Manchester United . The Reds sit 18th and are without a win in the Premier League for eight games, but Mauricio Pochettino's appointment means it's a fresh start for the Reds. The Argentine will be thrown into an imperative clash against Liverpool on Sunday, one that may determine his destiny as United boss. The Reds then face Sporting CP just three days after, meaning rotation in the starting eleven is not just expected, but needed. This rotation leaves space for players to gain the attention of the new gaffer, so here are three players who could do just that. 1. Leny Yoro French centre-back Leny Yoro has had a precarious start to his career at Manchester United . The defender arrived from Rennes for an initial £52 million, but despite his obvious talent, he's yet to cement his place in the starting eleven. The 21-year-old found most of his form under Rúben Amorim, as he fit perfectly into the three-back system Amorim attempted to implement; this could repeat under Pochettino. The former Spurs and Chelsea manager seems to insert a similar system at every club he's been to, a simple 4-2-3-1 in defence that transitions into a 3-4-2-1 in attack. This tactic features two recognised centre-backs, with a midfielder dropping in between the two defenders, the wing-backs pushing forward, and the wingers inverting. It sounds complicated, but it's an adaptation of Antonio Conte's infamous title-winning Chelsea system in 2016/17. Yoro does not fit the mould of an offensive wingback; therefore, he naturally settles as one of the two centre-backs. In fact, Sully Talkz mentioned this on his socials, saying: "Just wait until he gets better coaching, and he doesn't need to play out of position". If we look at Yoro's stats from the 2025/26 Premier League season, he ranks in the 70th percentile in tackles, recoveries, and possessions won in the final third per 90 minutes. These are key attributes for an aggressive centre-back. But what's interesting is Yoro's possession stats: he averaged 45.18 successful passes and 10.28 line-breaking passes per 90 last season, which puts him above average. These stats prove he will become a key player under Pochettino; he's young and has the opportunity to learn under a great manager. Expect to see Yoro in the starting 11 on Sunday. item.description: Motorsport photo Lewis Hamilton subtly implied Charles Leclerc ’s “frame of mind” was to blame for their collision in Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix. Hamilton and Leclerc were sixth and seventh on lap 37 of the Nevadan race, only some two seconds adrift of race leader Max Verstappen , when the Monegasque dived down the inside in Turn 7. His front wheels were nearly alongside the Briton’s, but he seemingly saw the door closing and backed out; as a result, his front axle was next to Hamilton’s sidepod at the apex and he ended up clipping his team-mate’s rear-left wheel, sending the sister car into a spin. This netted Leclerc a 10-second penalty, while Hamilton lost four positions and about eight seconds. As a consequence, they ended up respectively 10th and seventh under the chequered flag, missing out on a likely top five and a potential podium finish. This was just one of many incidents involving the Ferrari drivers this season, including their prominent clash on lap one of the Mexican Grand Prix, as they were running 1-2 and lost victory to Max Verstappen – which had prompted Hamilton to demand “serious talks”. Talks did occur, but three weeks on, the situation persists. Asked what was next following the Las Vegas incident – before he got a chance to discuss the issue with his team-mate – Hamilton elusively responded: “I don't know, but that's not something I want to get into. item.description: Gavin Sheets (L), Jackson Merrill (R) (Image from - IMAGN) The San Diego Padres and Gavin Sheets agreed to an $11 million extension, including a $500,000 signing bonus and a $2.5 million salary in 2027, ESPN’s Jeff Passan said. The deal also includes player options for the second and third years at $4 million each. The agreement will keep the Padres infielder in San Diego through the 2029 season. Sheets can test free agency earlier if he uses his player option in his second or third year. Fans reacted to the extension between Sheets and San Diego. “He needs to fire his agent, lol. Sheets has become an important part of the Padres lineup since joining the team in February 2025 on a minor league contract. In 2025, he finished with a .252 batting average, 19 home runs, 71 RBIs, and 28 doubles in 145 games. He followed that up with 17 home runs and 48 RBIs in 125 games during 2026. Sheets can play left field and first base, and he brings a valuable left-handed power bat. He is widely recognized in Petco Park with the famous “Ho-ly Sheets!” chant whenever he comes to the plate. Padres GM Reportedly Drops Insight On Gavin Sheets’ Injury The only concern about Gavin Sheets entering his final year of arbitration was his 2026 foot injury, which prompted a statistical decline. item.title: Taylor impressed with Exeter City's Oldham comeback
item.description: Matt Taylor's Exeter City side have won five of their last seven League Two games [Shutterstock] Exeter City manager Matt Taylor has said he was impressed with how his side came back to draw 1-1 at Oldham Athletic in League Two. The Grecians went 1-0 down during a poor first-half showing, but rallied after the break to secure a point. The result meant eighth-placed Exeter remain outside the play-off places on goal difference. They have lost just one of their past eight league games, having been one point off the relegation places before the start of their recent good run. "I'm pleased with the point because we were second best for large parts of the first half - second half was a much more even affair," he told BBC Radio Devon. "We've learnt a little bit today - we spoke before the game about what I was expecting, I don't think it shocked the players, but we were just second best too often in duels, in transitional moments, in second ball moments. "They seemed to go through our team too often, without creating chance after chance, and it's still a massive deflection for their goal. "But the way we came back into it second half and got the equaliser and then were pushing for a winner, I think speaks volumes of the character of the group." Oldham Athletic 1-1 Exeter City Exeter boss Taylor wants more settled transfer window Taylor said many of his young squad are yet to have much experience of difficult away games at the likes of Oldham. But he feels Saturday's draw will be a great boost for his players and show the club's fans how the side is coming on as they aim to mount a title challenge having been relegated last season and seen the bulk of their established first team squad move elsewhere. "I think they can start to not just believe in the team, but see what we're trying to do," he said. "Even today when we were second best for large parts, they stuck with us and that second half was exactly what we want our team to look like away from home. "As much as I've learnt today and the players have learnt, I think our fans have seen a little reminder of where we're at because we've gone on a great run and we get all the plaudits on the back of it. item.title: Before Gilchrist and Sangakkara, there was Les Ames: England great with 102 centuries whose record Rishabh Pant broke in Wellington
item.description: Box-office Rishabh Pant was at his brutal best against New Zealand in the first Test in Wellington, scoring 128 off 153 balls to register his ninth Test century. With this hundred, Pant became the sixth Indian batter to score a Test century in all four SENA countries, joining Mohammad Azharuddin, Sachin Tendulkar, Rahul Dravid, Virat Kohli and KL Rahul. Pant also climbed to second place on the list of most sixes in Test cricket, going past former New Zealand batter Brendon McCullum. He hit six sixes during his knock to take his tally to 108, one more than McCullum's 107. England's Ben Stokes leads the list with 138 sixes. The century also took Pant to third place on the list of most Test hundreds by a designated wicketkeeper. He moved past former England wicketkeeper Les Ames, who had scored eight centuries in 47 Tests. Pant now has nine hundreds, with only Adam Gilchrist (17) and Andy Flower (12) ahead of him. Most Test hundreds as a designated wicketkeeper 17 - Adam Gilchrist 12 - Andy Flower 9 - Rishabh Pant 8 - Les Ames Who was Les Ames? Leslie Ethelbert George Ames died suddenly at his home in Canterbury on February 26, 1990, aged 84. Ames passed away before Adam Gilchrist, Andy Flower and Kumar Sangakkara made their mark in the game. In his obituary, Wisden described him as someone who “was without a doubt the greatest wicketkeeper-batsman the game has so far produced.” Ames averaged more than 40 in Test cricket and scored eight centuries in 47 matches. He was considered the best batter among regular wicketkeepers of his time, ahead of players such as Jeff Dujon. When fully fit, Ames was England's first-choice wicketkeeper from 1931 to 1939, when he virtually gave up the role. He scored 2,434 runs in 47 Tests for England and was involved in 97 dismissals, including 74 catches and 23 stumpings. Ames toured Australia with M.C.C. in 1928-29 as reserve wicketkeeper to Duckworth. He was expected to play in the final Test at Melbourne as a specialist batter, but a broken finger while keeping to Larwood ruled him out. He made his Test debut against South Africa at The Oval in 1929. His final Test appearance came against South Africa in Durban in 1939. An efficient wicketkeeper Ames was popular with spectators across the country, but praise and attention did not affect him. He remained focused on his game and maintained a consistent standard behind the stumps. Among his notable performances for England were eight dismissals against West Indies at The Oval in 1933. During the 1938-39 series against South Africa, he conceded only one bye for every 275 balls delivered. On the Bodyline tour, he handled the fast bowling of Harold Larwood and Bill Voce with quiet efficiency. His wicketkeeping style was simple, with no flamboyant gestures. His glovework was neat and economical, while his stumpings were described as almost apologetic. item.title: Man Utd captain Bruno Fernandes shares fresh details on failed Tottenham transfer and Mauricio Pochettino talks
item.description: Manchester United v Aston Villa FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has shed new light on the sliding doors moment that almost saw him join Tottenham Hotspur instead of the Red Devils. The Portuguese international was on the verge of a move to north London in 2019, where he would have linked up with current United boss Mauricio Pochettino. How a 2019 Spurs transfer fell through Seven years after nearly uniting in north London, Fernandes is finally set to play under Pochettino at club level. Back in 2019, the Portugal star was plying his trade at Sporting when Tottenham made a concrete push to bring him to England. Discussions progressed far enough for the then 24-year-old to hold face-to-face meetings with Spurs officials and tour their facilities. However, the transfer collapsed during the closing days of that summer's window, leaving Fernandes in Portugal until Manchester United secured his signature in January 2020. Fernandes details talks with Tottenham's board Speaking to Sky Sports , Fernandes recalled how thoroughly Tottenham pitched their project to him during those negotiations. He noted that club chiefs outlined both their playing style and the specific tactical role Pochettino envisaged for him. "I met with the Tottenham board, I’ve met with all of them,” the 32-year-old said. "They showed me all the good things they had in their training ground, the way they wanted to play. They showed me also the positions that the manager has told them I could play in the system." Why playing alongside Spurs' stars appealed to Fernandes Asked whether Pochettino's tactical ideas won him over, the United captain admitted he was eager to test himself in England's top flight at that stage of his career. The opportunity to link up with an established attacking core made north London a particularly attractive destination. “Yeah, they were good. Obviously, I was a very young player, I was 24. I was eager to come to the Premier League. They had [Harry] Kane, they had Dele Alli, they have Son [Heung-min] there, they chance to play with those players in front was very attractive.” Once the deal broke down late in the window, Fernandes continued to impress in Portugal before completing his move to Manchester just months later. Pochettino faces high-stakes debut against Liverpool Fernandes and Pochettino finally join forces at Manchester United this weekend, with the skipper set to lead the side out on Sunday. With United sitting 18th in the table, the new manager faces an immediate test of pressure and expectation. Making his debut against arch-rivals Liverpool raises the stakes even further as Pochettino looks to spark a swift turnaround.

They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter.
